title: Microproof Concierge Surge Cookbook (wip)
body:
Purpose: lightweight, tactical recipe book sellers + SEs use to run a rapid concierge surge when a microproof/pilot is at risk. Focus is <48–72h triage + 2-week stabilization plan. Meant to be used live in Slack and during 1:1 customer rescue calls.

Quick elevator (what to say to buyer in 30s):
- "Hi — we see latency/cost/regression hitting your pilot. We’ll run a short concierge surge: dedicated SE + ops on-call will run tests, apply a two-step fallback, and deliver a clear scope of changes within 48 hours to get your pilot back to target."
- Ask: permission to run a low-risk canary (1% traffic) and a short token/trace capture for diagnostics.

When to start concierge surge (trigger checklist):
- Pilot error rate > 2% on critical routes OR
- 95th latency > target SLA by >2x for >30 minutes OR
- Unit cost deviation > 50% vs baseline AND customer escalation flagged OR
- Customer success escalates with imminent demo/exec review in next 72h.

First 2-hour rapid triage (owner: SE + on-call SRE):
1) Gather: customer org, routes impacted, sample request ids, recent config changes, model versions, deployment zone. (Scripted ask to CS: "Send these 3 request ids + last 24h traces")
2) Baseline repro: run minimal synthetic through the same route (provide sample payload below). Measure cold vs warm, KV-hit rate, batch sizes.
3) Quick config audit: quantization profile, batching policy, cache TTLs, routing rules (fallbacks on?).
4) If reproducible: capture 1 reproducible sample and escalate to Applied ML if model-quality suspected.
5) If no repro: enable traffic capture (redact PII) for 24h and schedule deeper dive.

Sample minimal payload (SE test):
- API: /v1/generate (hosted)
- model: rwd-13b-v2-quant (or customer pinned model)
- prompt: "Summarize the below 30-word paragraph in 1 sentence" + sample paragraph
- max_tokens: 60
- stream: false
- headers: include x-customer-route id + debug: true

Quick tactical mitigations (apply in this order, low-risk first):
- 1) Route traffic to warm pool (if available) — reduces cold-start latency. Impact: small increase in reserved cost.
- 2) Reduce max_tokens/response sampling for pilot traffic only (e.g., max_tokens -25%). Impact: lower unit cost, slightly shorter responses.
- 3) Turn on KV-prefix caching for repeated prompts. Impact depends on workload.
- 4) Temporarily pin a smaller model variant (e.g., rwd-6b) for non-critical demo routes. Communicate quality tradeoff.
- 5) If model regression suspected, fallback to verified-stable model bundle (rwd-13b-stable) and schedule quality postmortem.

Acceptance criteria for 48h surge success: (pick 2 of 3)
- 95th latency back within SLA or <1.5x target
- Error rate reduced to <1% on critical routes
- Unit cost decreased by >=25% vs peak OR customer confirms demo-ready

Communication templates (copy/paste)
- Slack to CS channel (first message):
  "Starting concierge surge for {{customer}}. SE: @Priya, SRE on-call: @Omar. Initial triage window 0–2h. Will post repro test and mitigation plan within 2h. Please DM 3 sample request ids and the most recent deploy changelist."
- Customer email (post-triage summary):
  "Hi {{name}}, thanks for the call. Summary: we reproduced the issue (latency error) on route X. Immediate action: shifted demo traffic to warm pool and reduced max_tokens for the demo route. Impact: expected 35% latency reduction and small output-shortening. Next steps: apply prefix cache and monitor for 48h. We'll send daily updates at 10am PT."

Escalation ladder (who to pull in):
- SE escalation: @Marco Alvarez (platform integrator)
- Applied ML: @Lena Park (model triage)
- Serving runtime on-call: #sre-oncall (use pager after 2h)
- Product owner (if config/design change needed): @Rita Gomez

Data to collect for post-mortem (urgent):
- Request ids + traces
- Model/version and quantization profile
- Batch/sequence length distribution (last 24h)
- Cost per token on impacted routes (last 24h vs baseline)
- Any autoscaler events or preemption notices

Two-week stabilization blueprint (owner: CS + SE)
- Day 0–2: triage + apply tactical mitigations (this doc)
- Day 3–7: roll targeted optimizations (kv caching, adjusted batching, runtime flags), track quality with prompt-sweep tests
- Day 8–14: performance tuning and optional dedicated capacity + SLA proposal. Confirm rollout window and sign-off.

Sales/Commercial asks to secure commitment:
- Offer a 2-week free concierge period for pilot customers who sign reserved capacity LOI (short-term incentive). Draft LOI language in linked_artifacts.
- If pilot-critical demo is saved, capture testimonial + brief case snippet within 7 days.

Quick decision matrix (one-pager logic):
- If regression in model quality -> involve Applied ML, fallback to stable-bundle, do not change model variant for demo unless approved by SE + PM.
- If latency-only and cost worry -> favor batching/pinning smaller models + report cost delta to procurement.
- If intermittent and not reproducible -> enable trace capture + increase debug sampling; do not change live routes until we have a trace.

Common objections and scripts:
- "We can’t change model during the demo" -> "We won’t change the default model for core flows; we’ll route demo traffic to an isolated canary with a clearly labeled quality note so your demo stays intact while we investigate."
- "This will break our SLAs" -> "Temporary canary and warm-pool shifts are reversible within minutes; we’ll coordinate exact windows and monitor together."

Notes to self / TODOs:
- add small table with expected cost delta numbers per mitigation (rough cents/token estimates) -- Marco to supply by 11/20.
- build a one-click playbook in Console to shift demo routes to warm-pool (feature request: GT-6320).
- create short video (90s) sellers can share explaining concierge surge.

Appendix: quick links
- Tracing guide: CONFLUENCE:serving-runtime/tracing
- Canary checklist (internal): CONFLUENCE:canary-checklist-v2
- Relevant Jira: JIRA:GT-6128 (pilot rescue), JIRA:INF-7402 (kv cache improvements)

End of doc -- keep terse, update with real numbers after next rescue run.
